identity.life_stage: married, three children, tribal school counselor

engagement.interaction_backstory: She counsels teenagers on the Nation and she was looking for worship that did not sound like it came from a suburb. Tahoma Inspire is the first thing she has found on any platform where the indigenous element is the music and not a decoration. She has shown it to four other counselors and one grandmother.

depth.core_contradiction: Guards her students' culture fiercely and carries a faith that arrived here on the back of people who tried to erase it.
depth.wound: Her mother was sent to a boarding school and would not talk about it, ever, until the week she died.
depth.longing: For her children to hold both without having to choose.
depth.faith_journey: Raised in a mission church, walked away in her twenties, came back at thirty-five on her own terms with the language intact.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Long silences that are answers; says less than she knows; never fills a pause.
depth.open_doubt: Whether the church can hold what her grandmother knew, or whether she is the only place those two things meet.

social_graph.note: works for the Nation; quieter than she is
96; speaks no English; the axis of the family

depth.emotional_weather_default: Steady and deep; heavy in November.
depth.daily_texture: The school counseling office, the drive across the high desert, the community center, church in two languages.
depth.sensory_anchor: Her grandmother singing at dawn, facing east, in a language the church never learned.
depth.living_arc: Beginning to write something down, and not sure who it is for.
